properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 10:56AM CDT until August 7 at 2:31AM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Moderate flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue falling to 7.8 feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 30.9
feet on 06/07/2021.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 5 at 1:13PM EDT until August 5 at 5:15PM EDT by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
FFWPHI

The National Weather Service in Mount Holly has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Gloucester County in southern New Jersey...
Eastern Delaware County in southeastern Pennsylvania...
South Central Montgomery County in southeastern Pennsylvania...
Western Philadelphia County in southeastern Pennsylvania...

* Until 515 PM EDT.

* At 113 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain moving into the
warned area. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have fallen across portions
of the area. The expected rainfall rate is 0.5 to 1 inch in 30
minutes. Additional rainfall amounts up to 2 inches are possible
in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rain.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets, and underpasses as well as other
drainage and low lying areas.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Philadelphia, Gloucester City, Chester, Deptford, West Deptford,

and Westville.

Interstate 95 in Pennsylvania between mile markers 4 and 17.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 5 at 10:00AM CDT until August 5 at 1:15PM CDT by NWS Des Moines IA
properties.description:

flooding in the Murray area in western Clarke County around 840 am,
with more than six inches of water flowing over some roads, where
the heaviest rain occurred. Although floodwaters are likely on their
way down, flash flooding remains possible especially in lower areas
or areas small streams and other drainage areas.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Osceola, Corydon, Lakeside Casino, Murray, Seymour, Allerton,
Humeston, Van Wert, Garden Grove, Woodburn, Weldon, Derby,
Millerton, Le Roy and Murray Roadside Rest Area.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 5 at 5:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Petersville Area

* WHEN...Until 500 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Low-water
crossings are inundated with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated scattered rain showers continue across the warned
area. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.
Between 2 and 3 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts of up to 0.5 inches are possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 PM AKDT THIS AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued August 5 at 4:18AM AKDT until August 7 at 1:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Yentna River including Lake Creek.

* WHEN...Until 100 PM AKDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Streams
continue to rise due to excess runoff from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 359 AM AKDT, The river gauge at the Yentna River at Lake
Creek indicates rises in water levels from heavy rain across
the warned area. Flooding is ongoing. Trees and debris larger
than telephone poles have been observed flowing down the
river. Between 1.0 and 2.5 inches of rain have fallen.
Additional rainfall amounts of up to 0.5 inch are possible
with higher amounts possible in the upper Yentna Basin.
- For Yentna River at Lake Creek:
At 3:50am the stage was 22.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 20.5 feet.
Forecast: Cresting Wednesday morning above 22 feet.

Impacts:
Between 21 and 22 feet, several lodges may have water in or
around low-lying cabins.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
